To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) We collect a dataset of 14,000 conversations with knowledge-grounding annotations.

we collect and release the WikiDial dataset, a large-scale dataset for open domain dialogue, which is grounded with knowledge retrieved directly from Wikipedia, and design a model architecture that is capable of retrieving knowledge from Wikipedia and using it for generating natural responses.

(a) knowledge is useful to the performance of a conversational agent; (b) knowledge can be retrieved, read and used by neural models; and (c) the new dataset we release is a useful tool for future research in this area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing knowledge-grounded dialogue models that can converse about topics of interest, using knowledge as context.

the following three questions: 1) What is the best way to retrieve and condition on knowledge in dialogue? 2) How to evaluate knowledge-powered dialogue systems? 3) Can we build knowledge-powered dialogue systems that can conduct knowledgeable discussions on topics of interest?

the following questions: 1) How to design architectures for knowledge-powered open-domain dialogue? 2) How to evaluate the knowledge grounding in dialogue systems? 3) How to collect and annotate a large-scale dataset with knowledge grounded conversations?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we are able to create a knowledge-powered dialogue model that can conduct knowledgeable discussions on topics of open-domain, and that our new dataset will allow for further improvements in this direction.

we have created a new dataset, and a new model architecture which allows the use of external knowledge for open domain dialogue, and which outperforms the previous state of the art in both automatic and human evaluation.
our work is a step towards building more human-like conversational agents that can use knowledge in open domain conversations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to demonstrate that knowledge can be successfully used to generate natural language responses, and we provide a new benchmark to measure further improvements in this research direction.
We introduce WikiDial, a new benchmark dataset for open-domain knowledge-powered dialogue.

we are the first to show that a knowledge-based dialogue model can outperform a generic dialogue model on both automatic and human evaluation, while being able to generate more coherent and informative responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
knowledge is indeed useful and should be incorporated in the next generation of open-domain dialogue systems.
it is indeed possible to create a system which is able to converse about a topic by retrieving and conditioning on knowledge from Wikipedia.
it is now possible to build knowledge-powered dialogue agents, and that the field should now focus on improving the quality and quantity of knowledge available in these systems.
